summary_paragraph: A young woman with congenital tracheomalacia and tracheostomy status was admitted for recurrent chills, pleuritic chest pain, and dark green, blood-tinged sputum two days after completing a course of vancomycin for MRSA tracheitis. She had a recent history of Staph lugdunensis bacteremia and chronic respiratory issues. Evaluation showed no pneumonia on chest X-ray, negative blood cultures, and sputum with only rare commensal flora. The infectious disease team concluded she did not have an acute infection. Instead, symptoms were attributed to airway irritation likely due to inadequate humidification. Antibiotics were discontinued, and the interventional pulmonary team reinforced the use of a daily Portex Thermovent® HME during the day and a humidified trach mask at night. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with care coordination for supplies and follow-up with pulmonology, ENT, and infectious disease. Her chronic iron deficiency anemia remained stable on supplementation, with hemoglobin electrophoresis still pending.
